title: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction
abstract: Continuous quantum error correction promises reduced thresholds and hardware overhead compared to the digital paradigm, but its complex model estimation has greatly reduced its practicality. We recast this problem as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy made of an exact bilinear reduced model, an exact conditional filter, and standard estimation and feedback design. For any $[[n,k,d]]$ stabilizer code whose generators are all continuously monitored and which is driven by a single Pauli recovery channel, we prove that the exact filter closes at dimension $3\cdot2^{\,n-k-1}$. This dimension is set by the syndrome space instead of the Hilbert space and is minimal within invariant-subspace filtering. The reduced model exposes and corrects two failure mechanisms of the feedback loop. Strong monitoring damps the rotational partner through which the controller steers the stabilizer and injects back-action diffusion along the recovery path; lowering the measurement strength during correction raises the entanglement fidelity of partner-steering LQR control by $0.096$ in the three-qubit code with three monitored parities. Linearizing at the codespace leaves the syndrome uncontrollable, so the controller can stall; a gain designed at a shifted operating point removes this degeneracy. In the limit of zero measurement during correction, we prove that a syndrome-only filter is exact at every recovery boundary. The resulting committed-recovery controller needs only $2^{\,n-k}$ class probabilities and gives the highest entanglement fidelity compared among the methods tested in the literature, $0.947$ against $0.920$ for a measurement-based estimator protocol in the three-qubit bit-flip code, and $0.726$ vs at most $0.407$ for continuous controllers in the five-qubit perfect code.
authors: Manuel Guatto; F. A. Cárdenas-López; Felix Motzoi

title: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
abstract: Terrestrial free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) provides a flexible complement to fiber-based networks, but its deployment over long horizontal paths in dense metropolitan environments remains challenging, as atmospheric turbulence, demanding pointing and tracking requirements, and operational constraints can substantially increase system complexity. We experimentally demonstrate the operation of a decoy-state BB84 system over an 18.9~km free-space link across a densely populated urban area in the metropolitan region of Barcelona using an aviation-compliant optical architecture. The system operates at 785~nm using room-temperature single-photon detectors and requires no adaptive optics at the receiver. The modular QKD transmitter, based on a deployment-oriented design, is interfaced with a versatile free-space optical terminal and an independent GPS-disciplined synchronization architecture, facilitating its integration into heterogeneous optical infrastructures. We present the transmitter performance and optical-link characteristics, together with a 40-minute field test characterized by an average channel attenuation of approximately 19~dB and a mean QBER of 1.31\%. From the measured channel parameters, we estimate an average finite-size secret key rate exceeding 11~kbit/s. These results demonstrate the feasibility of inter-city free-space QKD over dense urban areas using a comparatively simple architecture.
authors: Ignacio H. López Grande; Nicolas Linale; Giacomo Paganini; Achraf El Bouazzaoui; Adrián S. Blanca; Ilektra Karakosta-Amarantidou; Manu Canals i Codina; Adam Vallés; Andrea Gorni; Jorge Fuenzalida; Evelyn A. Ortega; Valerio Pruneri

title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
abstract: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.
authors: Yuji Ando; Edmund Chen; Go Kato; Toyohiro Tsurumaru; Derek Zhang; Donald Zvada

title: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics
abstract: Driving lattice vibrations provides a direct route to manipulating electronic correlations through nonlinear electron-phonon coupling. Finding suitable driving fields, however, requires control over the coupled dynamics beyond a simple choice of pulse amplitude and frequency. Here we develop a differentiable framework that combines field optimization with neural-network prediction in a two-site electron-phonon model. We compare piecewise-constant, B-spline, feed-forward, and recurrent control parameterizations, optimized to increase the accumulated electronic double occupation. For the dissipation-free model at zero Hubbard interaction, all the methods increase double occupation, with the B-spline raising the mean total double occupation of approximately 30%. Alongside control optimization, a separate recurrent network learns to predict the next-step double occupation and phonon observables from their preceding values and the applied field. These results establish a computational proof of concept for shaping local electronic correlations through a phonon drive and identify a promising route toward learned models for nonequilibrium materials control.
authors: Matteo Puviani

title: Non-Convex Optimization via Quantum Tunneling Search on a Photonic Chip
abstract: Non-convex optimization plays an important role in modern machine learning since plenty of real-world problems have objective functions or constraints with non-convex properties. The non-convex nature of landscapes gives rise to numerous local minima and saddle points, dramatically hindering the ability of gradient descent-based methods to explore the landscape and obtain global optima. Here we present quantum tunneling search (QTS), an algorithm based on quantum tunneling walk and local annealing, which effectively explores the non-convex landscape by leveraging the quantum tunneling effect. In experiments, we map an objective function to the potential term of the waveguide Hamiltonian by controlling the refractive index with the femtosecond direct laser writing technique. With a proper input state, the average probability distributions on 10-micrometer-spaced 29 x 1 and 21 x 9 waveguide arrays highlight the local minima of various 1D and 2D non-convex landscapes, respectively. By further introducing the varying Hamiltonian approach, more efficient search and even the identification of the global minimum are achieved. Our work experimentally verifies that QTS is a successful and efficient non-convex optimization solver, demonstrating quantum speedups over classical stochastic gradient descent (SGD), which serves as a practical application of near-term analog quantum simulators in the field of machine learning.
authors: Xi-Jun Yuan; Shuo Zhou; Yizhou Liu; Xuan Chen; Hong-Jing Du; Xiao-Wen Shang; Wen-Hao Zhou; Yu-Xuan Fu; Bao-Jing Liu; Ze-Feng Lan; Hang Song; Fang-Song Nie; Yu-Lin Yu; Xiao-Yun Xu; Jian-Peng Dou; Tongyang Li; Hao Tang; Xian-Min Jin

title: Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like interference between two independent narrowband thermal states
abstract: Narrowband photonic sources are promising candidates in quantum networks for a direct interface with atomic quantum memories. However, building a large-scale quantum network requires many indistinguishable sources, and matching the frequencies of independent narrowband sources is generally challenging. Here, we propose a method to measure the frequency difference between two narrowband light sources in the single-photon power regime by studying Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like (HOM) interference between thermal states. Our results show that the absolute value of the frequency difference can be extracted from the temporal coincidence counts, and these results agree well with our theoretical model. We also demonstrate that the beat signal of the HOM-like interference between two thermal states has a similar oscillation profile to the HOM interference between two heralded single-photon sources, confirming that this method can be used to find the zero detuning of two heralded single-photon sources.
authors: Sheng-Hsuan Huang; Thomas Dirmeier; Andrea Aiello; Kaisa Laiho; Dmitry V. Strekalov; Gerd Leuchs; Christoph Marquardt

title: Quantum Keynesian Beauty Contest with Continuous Variables
abstract: The development of quantum computing has opened up opportunities to re-explore conventional game models by the integration of quantum processes. Through the established framework of quantum game theory, we examine the problem of speculative pricing in the Keynesian Beauty Contest model -- the $p$-Beauty Contest ($p$-BC). In the $p$-BC, players are rewarded with the optimal payoff for successfully bidding at some fraction $p$ of the average of all of the players' bids. Consequently, \textit{rational} plays in the $p$-BC inexorably lead to boom or bust strategies for $p>1$ or $p<1$ respectively. We demonstrate a quantum continuous-variable implementation of $p$-BC where the boom-and-bust rational behavior is mitigated through a global transformation of the players' bids generated by increasing multimode squeezing. While we focus on a quantum mechanical implementation of the $p$-BC, we show that an entirely analogous game can be formulated via classical channels by a global mediator. Thus we identify global mediation as the underlying game-theoretic mechanism for quenching boom and bust phenomena in our model. We analyze the quantum $p$-BC for two, three, and many players in a mean-field type implementation. We derive an analytical form for the probability distribution of the payoff under single-value measurements of the quantum processing circuit, and explore how the rational behavior differs from the expected-value measurement setting.
authors: Hiu Ming Lau; Kareem Raslan; Kieran Hymas; Qiang Sun; Azhar Iqbal; Derek Abbott; James Q. Quach; Andrew D. Greentree

title: The landscape of quantum technology companies in 2026
abstract: We update our 2022 mapping of 441 quantum technology (QT) companies and examine how the industry has developed. The principal dataset now includes 1,092 companies founded with a QT focus, of which 935 remain active. Public sources and archived company websites provide evidence on company formation, technology fields and geography, alongside acquisitions, closures, valuations and involvement in artificial intelligence, defence and space. Company formation continued beyond the apparent 2018 peak in the earlier study. Computing software and applications remain the largest field, with suppliers and supporting businesses accounting for almost a third of active companies. Countries with similar company totals can have different technological profiles, and regional comparisons reveal concentrations obscured by country rankings. The first companies generally preceded the selected national policy milestones. Supporting businesses usually followed technical companies in the same jurisdiction. AI is more prevalent than defence in current company activities, while defence shows the larger increase from the earliest assessed evidence. Space relevance is documented for more than a quarter of active companies, often alongside defence involvement.
authors: Zeki Can Seskir; Orcun Kocak; Arsev Umur Aydinoglu

title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.
authors: Sizhe Yan; Biao Wu

title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory
abstract: A large body of work in quantum machine learning has centered on characterizing the expressivity and performance of quantum models. In contrast, little attention has been paid to the reliability of predictions beyond average performance measures such as accuracy. In this work, we introduce an uncertainty-aware quantum classification framework based on Dempster-Shafer theory. This theory allows to express uncertainty through weights assigned not only to individual classification labels but to sets of labels. We introduce a training strategy that enables parameterized quantum circuits to learn such assignments directly from data. This provides an efficient way to prepare the corresponding quantum states and enables the application of different post-processing strategies. In particular, it offers a practical setting for quantum Dempster-Shafer fusion procedures with polynomial resource requirements, even when the corresponding mass functions are defined over exponentially many subsets. Overall, our work represents a step toward enabling quantum models to express uncertainty about their predictions, thereby extending the evaluation of quantum models beyond predictive performance alone.
authors: Marie Kempkes; Jakob Spiegelberg; Evert van Nieuwenburg; Vedran Dunjko

title: Symmetry-Controlled Criticality and Zeno Localization in a Monitored Quasiperiodic Superconductor
abstract: Measurement-induced transitions of free fermions depend strongly on symmetry, but their interplay with quasiperiodic localization and superconducting pairing remains largely unexplored. We study a continuously monitored model of free fermions with pairing, where quasiperiodicity both controls localization and changes the symmetry class of the monitored field theory. Using topological entanglement entropy as a probe of nonlocal correlations in quantum state diffusion simulations, we identify a transition between a critical phase whose von Neumann entanglement entropy scales as $(\ln L)^2$ and an area-law phase, whereas no transition occurs in the clean limit, consistent with the corresponding DIII and D nonlinear sigma models. The transition line exhibits strong multifractality and depends nonmonotonically on quasiperiodicity, which we associate with the symmetry crossover. Deep in the Zeno regime, we derive an effective non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes description of individual trajectories and obtain a closed-form localization length that quantitatively agrees with numerics. Our results reveal how symmetry, quasiperiodic localization, and measurement backaction combine to determine both critical entanglement and microscopic trajectory localization in monitored superconductors.
authors: Pinaki Singha; Marcin Szyniszewski; Nilanjan Roy; Auditya Sharma

title: When can local unitaries generate a complete orthogonal basis?
abstract: The question of local encodability asks: can a given, multipartite pure quantum state be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations? If any such state in a given system has this property, it is called universally locally encodable (ULE), a feature, which has applications in quantum information theory, engineering and math. Despite its easy formulation, the answer to this question depends nontrivially on the local dimensions of the system: While universal local encodability is known for $2\times 2$, $4\times 4$ and $8\times 8$-dimensional systems, it was so-far only conjectured to hold in $3\times 3$, and non-ULE was recently proved for systems of four and more qubits by Pauwels and Gühne. We resolve the open conjecture by proving universality for two qutrits. Furthermore, we construct (among others) universal local encodings in dimensions $d\times2$ for $d\ge2$, in dimensions $d\times3$ for $d=3,4$ and $d\ge6$, and in every bipartite system with one or two infinite-dimensional subsystems. For finite-dimensional multipartite systems, we turn a heuristic parameter count into a necessary condition for universality, which excludes universal local encodability in infinitely many cases. Finally, we give universal local encodability an operational interpretation by showing that non-ULE is equivalent to whether general measurements yield an advantage over projectively simulable ones in discrimination tasks where unknown, random local unitary rotations have to be detected.
authors: Julian Eisfeld; Hermann Kampermann; Nikolai Wyderka

title: Squeezed terahertz light from nonlinear diamagnetism in ultrastrongly coupled two-dimensional electrons
abstract: Two-dimensional electron gases in terahertz cavities are among the most mature platforms for ultrastrong light--matter coupling, yet their collective response is captured by the linear Hopfield model, which has an exact classical correspondence. We show that the intrinsic band nonparabolicity of the electrons, recently revealed through nonlinear diamagnetism, turns this system into a quantum Kerr oscillator that squeezes terahertz light. Using a non-rotating-wave theory with ultrastrong-coupling-consistent input--output, an ab initio cavity bath, and a self-consistent model of electron heating, we predict output squeezing of 1.8--2.4\,dB with present GaAs samples in weakly confined cavities with quality factors of order $10^2$, and up to $\approx9$\,dB with modest improvements in mobility or cavity frequency. Carrier heating sets limits through a material figure of merit, which yields a simple design rule that the optimal cavity quality factor scales inversely with the ultrastrong-coupling strength.
authors: Dasom Kim; Junichiro Kono; Stephen Hughes

title: Communication Supremacy of a Qubit in Holevo Frenkel Weiner Scenario
abstract: The prevailing wisdom asserts that in the Holevo Frenkel Weiner (HFW) framework of communication tasks, a qubit offers no advantage over a c bit unless additional quantum resources are supplied or the classical shared randomness (SR) is restricted. In contrast, we establish the supremacy of qubit communication in the HFW framework when additional quantum resources, such as entanglement or measurement incompatibility are not injected and SR is a free resource. We consider a prepare-measure scenario where the sender, Alice, prepares six states subject to a specific cryptographic constraint, and the receiver, Bob, performs a three-outcome measurement. Such a constraint on preparation impacts the power of qubit communication quite differently than that of c-bit communication, ultimately giving rise to the quantum advantage. We introduce a witness capable of distinguishing quantum strategies that lie beyond the set of possible classical strategies and demonstrate the optimal quantum advantage. {As an application, we demonstrate the generation of certified randomness without requiring any seed randomness, since Bob has no input.} We further analyse the robustness of the witness and show that the advantage persists in noisy situations, making it suitable for experimental realisation. Finally, we demonstrate that Bob's three outcome qubit positive operator valued-measure (POVMs) has a distinct capability of detecting coherence, which can be regarded as the non-classical feature responsible for showcasing the quantum advantage.
authors: Partha Patra; Sumit Mukherjee; A. K. Pan

title: Unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems: Derivation, dynamics, and spectral signatures
abstract: Drive-modified dissipation in multilevel quantum systems is not, in general, accurately captured by conventional master equations. We derive a unified master equation using Lewis-Riesenfeld dynamical invariants, accommodating arbitrary driving within Born-Markov theory. We demonstrate the applicability of the unified master equation to constant-Rabi-coupling (continuous-wave), periodically-modulated-Rabi-coupling, and nonperiodic (ramped and chirped) driving protocols. Fluorescence spectra of a periodically driven three-level $Λ$ system reveal signatures missed by conventional descriptions. We trace the limitations of the conventional descriptions to inaccurate bath-frequency sampling and the neglect of nonsecular dissipative couplings, and map out the parameter regimes that require a unified treatment. The fluorescence spectra provide experimentally accessible signatures, which serve as a spectroscopic guide to reliable modeling of dissipative processes that can inform quantum control, simulation, sensing, and information processing.
authors: Sagarika Basak; D. Blume

title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
abstract: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.
authors: Chen Yang; Yu-An Chen

title: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
abstract: In solids, the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), $Q_{μν}=g_{μν}-\frac{i}{2} Ω_{μν}$, combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Its imaginary part governs anomalous velocity and quantized Hall transport, while its real part determines the quantum weight and geometric contributions to flat-band superfluid stiffness and dielectric response. Here, we extend the QGT to four-dimensional (4D) energy-momentum space ($ω/c,k$), treating frequency and momentum as independent coordinates. Invariance of the real-spacetime plane-wave phase fixes their Lorentz transformation in energy-momentum space. Lorentz boosts of static Dirac and Weyl systems then generate frequency metrics, quadrupolar frequency-momentum shear metrics, and electric-like Berry-Maxwell fields. We identify five Lorentz-invariant contractions and derive the governing field equations and flow conservation laws for both the quantum metric and Berry curvature from static Weyl geometry and Lorentz covariance. We further connect Gaussian spectral amplitudes of the QGT to localized Gaussian events in 4D spacetime. Finally, we discuss experimental realizations in spacetime crystals or time-varying media and clarify how this unified quantum geometry of a gravitational-like metric and electromagnetic-like gauge fields connects geometric self-consistency with physical event dynamics.
authors: Yiming Pan

title: Improved Low-Cost Quantum Error Mitigation with Benchmarked-Noise Zero-Noise Extrapolation (bnZNE)
abstract: We theoretically extend and experimentally demonstrate benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation (bnZNE), a simple and low-cost method for quantum error mitigation which aims to outperform the highly popular ZNE method for an equal total shot cost by improving the classical extrapolation step. We recently proposed bnZNE as a new error mitigation method (Harris et al., arXiv:2603.10224 (2026)) and showed that it can mitigate noise to the same order as standard ZNE under gate-wise depolarizing noise. Here, we introduce randomized bnZNE which addresses the case of running multiple random circuits per noise level, allowing for the incorporation of noise-tailoring techniques like Pauli twirling and readout error mitigation, and test the method on the IBM and IQM hardware for a plethora of large-scale applications, observing bnZNE to consistently produce more accurate results than standard ZNE. Our approach enhances the extrapolation process to the zero-noise limit by using classically-simulable and structure-mirroring benchmark circuits, generated from the standard application circuit, to sensitively measure the effective error rate at each scaled noise level beyond simple integer values. We give a new method for generating tailored benchmark circuits for the IQM superconducting devices and test them experimentally. Our results demonstrate that bnZNE presents a versatile alternative to ZNE which can enable more accurate results at utility scales with an equivalent cost.
authors: Joseph Harris; Kevin Lively; Peter Ken Schuhmacher

title: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
abstract: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator. In practice, we find that the criterion based on the second-order moments of the realigned operator is already sufficient to witness the entanglement of a wide range of quantum optical states. The realigned moments can be readily accessed using an optical scheme consisting of a linear interferometer that couples several identical copies of the state, similarly to the multicopy technique used to measure the partial-transpose moments of a state [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064 (2026)]. We illustrate the detection capability of the second-order realigned-moment method for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.
authors: Serge Deside; Vojtěch Kala; Nicolas J. Cerf

title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
abstract: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.
authors: Simon Kochsiek; Mario Boneberg; Igor Lesanovsky

title: Physical Observables and Superselection
abstract: It is well-known that a physical state may be represented by a unit vector in a Hilbert space, whilst a physical observable may be represented by a self-adjoint operator on that same space. However, the introduction of a superselection rule on a Hilbert space imposes constraints such that not all self-adjoint operators can represent observables, which has further consequences for the states themselves as well as the physical processes that transform them. In this article, we review the concept of superselection from the view of how such rules would affect what we consider to be physical. Arguments for the existence of a superselection rule due to charge or possibly energy conservation are given and the emergence of effective superselection rules due to decoherence or the lack of a shared reference frame are also discussed.
authors: Martin Paul Vaughan

title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
abstract: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with \(\hbar\). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.
authors: Fei Wang

title: Noise robust super-Heisenberg scaling in time-dependent quantum sensing by subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling
abstract: In quantum parameter estimation, time-dependent Hamiltonians can enable ultraprecise estimates of a physical parameter beyond the standard Heisenberg limit, also called the super-Heisenberg limit. However, achieving optimal scaling of the measurement precision typically requires an adaptive quantum control scheme which is resource-intensive and hard to implement in general. Furthermore, this advantage is often severely eroded by environmental noise. We propose the use of a dynamical decoupling scheme based on subspace twirling -- the averaging of random unitaries over a subspace rather than the entire Hilbert space -- to overcome these two limitations. We first prove necessary and sufficient conditions for subspace twirling to preserve the encoding signal while simultaneously removing environmental noise. We then establish conditions and provide performance guarantees for when time dependent Hamiltonians undergoing subspace twirling can achieve super-Heisenberg scaling without adaptive controls. Finally, we illustrate our results using an explicit example where a qubit sensor undergoing a subspace twirl simultaneously suppresses noise and achieves super-Heisenberg scaling. These results offer guidance for the design of ultraprecise quantum sensors under time-dependent and noisy conditions.
authors: Bakmou Lahcen; Ke Zeng; Tianyu Yang; Yu Jiang; Kok Chuan Tan

title: Gaussian ergotropy and spatial correlations: accelerated vacuum versus a thermal field
abstract: Can the spatial correlations of a quantum environment be revealed through work extraction? We address this question using two harmonic-oscillator detectors coupled to either an accelerated vacuum or a matched inertial thermal field. We establish a quantitative connection between the spatial correlations of the environment and the equilibrium Gaussian ergotropy, showing that the leading extractable work is governed by a response-weighted spatial correlation. Although the two environments have identical local spectra, their different spatial correlations give rise to distinct work responses. We further identify a finite-distance blind point at which a single measurement configuration fails to distinguish the two environments. By reversing the direct coupling between the detectors, we develop a two-setting scheme that removes this ambiguity and reconstructs the underlying spatial correlations from work measurements. This reconstruction remains effective beyond the weak-coupling regime. We also show that spatial correlations can provide additional global work even when the detector pair is separable, demonstrating that entanglement is not a necessary resource for this advantage. Finally, we investigate the transient evolution of Gaussian ergotropy and reveal its oscillatory decay and dependence on acceleration and detector parameters. Our results establish Gaussian ergotropy as an operational probe of spatial correlations in bosonic environments.
authors: Siwei Li; Xiaofen Huang; Shao-Ming Fei

title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
abstract: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator. We focus on the local interactions models, where the particles' states are modified only when two or more of them appear on the same grid site. The main focus is given to the two-dimensional grid in space. We study the dependence of the search algorithm asymptotic success time and probability on the interaction strength and the generated maximal entanglement between particles. We show that the interacting and non-interacting two- and three-particle search algorithm attains a constant factor improvement over the single-particle counterpart. In addition, we provide a new generalized model of interactions for multi-particle quantum walks.
authors: Gonçalo Meneses; D. O. Oriekhov

title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlevé VI
abstract: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlevé VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. For the Painlevé VI angular Hamiltonian these operators satisfy $[N,J_\pm]=\pm2kJ_\pm$, where $N=\sqrt M$, and close through an eighth-degree norm polynomial. Combining the angular shifts with the radial shift operators of the oscillator, Coulomb and free Bessel systems yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras for the two-dimensional superintegrable models. This construction provides new families of Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz (TTW)- and Post-Winternitz (PW)-like Hamiltonians with integrals of arbitrarily high order and Painlevé VI in the potential. This framework also recovers models from the classification of third- and fourth-order integrals as particular cases. For a representative oscillator extension we compute the Casimir explicitly and recover the finite-dimensional energy spectrum from a deformed-oscillator realization. We then analyze the special-solution sector using the explicit families collected by Gromak, Laine and Shimomura. The resulting potentials are organized into a small number of spectral classes, and the distinction between formal zeros of the ladder norm and physical self-adjoint representations is made explicit. The regular nonclassical rational examples are rational Darboux deformations of the trigonometric Pöschl--Teller system and lead to strictly isospectral exceptional-Jacobi sectors or to state-adding representations with an isolated angular level. A singular branch produces an interior inverse-square barrier and a split-domain problem. For one regular exceptional sector and two state-adding sectors we display the polynomial algebras.
authors: Ian Marquette; Anthony J. L. Parr

title: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies
abstract: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for quantum computation. For complex, entangled initial states it is, however, difficult to prepare shallow quantum circuits approximating the state with sufficient accuracy. Tensor networks provide a promising avenue of synthesis of such circuits, but most approaches employ 1D Matrix Products States, which struggle to accurately express entangled states in higher dimensions. Here we present a hardware topology-aware quantum state preparation method based on gradient optimization of 2D projected entangled pair states (PEPS). Our approach combines local disentanglement, with global fine tuning based on PEPS gradient optimization. Towards this end we describe an efficient procedure for PEPS gradient computation. We test the convergence and performance of our method in numerical simulations.
authors: Illia Lukin; Vladyslav Bohun; Maciej Koch-Janusz

title: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases
abstract: We develop a framework to study subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases using lattice response theory. We begin with a systematic construction of spacetime lattice gauge fields from general microscopic $X$-type symmetry actions on qudit systems, including global symmetries, subsystem symmetries, and more general modulated symmetries. Given a gauge-invariant response action, we then construct a corresponding entangler and explicitly show that it implements stacking with the SSPT phase described by the response action. We show that a broad class of SSPT phases can be described by intersection pairings and realized by cluster entanglers. We also study SSPT phases beyond intersection pairings, including those described by subsystem analogues of type-II group cocycles involving the Bockstein homomorphism. We construct a new 3+1d SSPT phase protected by two 2-foliated planar subsystem symmetries and a global 0-form symmetry, whose response action is a subsystem analogue of a type-III cocycle. On its boundary, the 0-form symmetry acts by stacking with a 2+1d linear SSPT phase, signaling a mixed 't Hooft anomaly.
authors: Yuki Furukawa; Takuya Okuda

title: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states are pure multipartite states with maximally mixed reductions on every set of at most half the parties. We construct explicit families in local dimension $2q$, twice an odd prime power $q$, using an established coupling of qubits and $q$-level systems. The $q$-level states remove interference between branches, so the qubit states need maximally mixed reductions only on average. This gives AME$(9,2q)$ and AME$(11,2q)$ for every odd prime power $q\geq5$, AME$(13,2q)$ for $q\geq17$, AME$(15,2q)$ for $q\geq9$, and AME$(17,2q)$ for $q\geq67$. For every odd $N\geq3$, the same coupling gives AME$(N,2q)$ under the sufficient condition $q\geq\max\{N,2^{N-2}\}$ on the odd prime power $q$. Within this coupling, the smallest such $q$ must grow exponentially with $N$. Combined with known inputs and products, these families complete the nine-party classification: for integer $d\geq2$, an AME$(9,d)$ state exists if and only if $d\geq3$. Choosing the branch pairing also gives AME$(15,2p)$ states with a cyclic shift of the parties compensated by local unitaries, for every prime $p\equiv1\pmod{15}$.
authors: Palash Pandya

title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
abstract: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.
authors: Romit Chakraborty

title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear. Here, we investigate a frozen, general-purpose LLM that generates complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions, with optional iterative energy feedback. We evaluate the approach on general random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, and molecular systems. For general Hamiltonians, LLM-generated parameters exhibit larger energy errors than conventional Adam optimization, while additional feedback generally provides limited improvement. In contrast, for structured Hamiltonians, the LLM can generate promising low-energy parameter configurations, suggesting that identifiable physical and mathematical structure facilitates parameter inference. We also show that direct LLM predictions of minimum energies can violate the Hamiltonian spectral lower bound, whereas generated circuit parameters allow independent evaluation of physically realizable energy expectation values. Finally, we investigate blind circuit interpretation and find that the LLM can predict measurement outcomes even when it fails to identify the underlying quantum algorithm. These findings highlight the role of problem structure, the limitations of iterative LLM optimization, and the importance of independently verifiable predictions in quantum parameter programming.
authors: Tiago de Souza Farias; Caio Moraes Porto; Matheus da Silva Fonseca; Nicolas Armando Cabrera Carpi; Anderson de Araujo Oliveira; Celso Jorge Villas-Boas

title: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections. Unidimensional (1D) Gaussian modulation offers a simpler alternative by encoding information in only one quadrature, while the conjugate quadrature constrains the protocol's security. However, an integrated experimental 1D implementation combining independent-laser coherent reception with practical reconciliation, finite-size parameter estimation, and privacy amplification remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD system over 12~km of standard single-mode fiber using a local local oscillator (LLO) architecture with independent lasers and an integrated offline classical post-processing chain. The implementation includes coherent detection, digital signal processing, information reconciliation, parameter estimation, physicality-constrained security analysis, and privacy amplification. The 1D system achieves a privacy-amplified rate of $1.421$~Mbit/s under the asymptotic security treatment and $0.364$~Mbit/s under the finite-size scenario. These results establish an experimental baseline for the performance--complexity trade-off associated with unidimensional Gaussian modulation and provide an experimental basis for developing lower-complexity CV-QKD transmitters.
authors: Christiano M. S. Nascimento; Maron F. Anka; Gabriel A. V. Menezes; Davi J. G. de Sousa; Nelson A. Neto; Artur A. Matoso; Gustavo C. Amaral; Valéria L. Silva; Guilherme P. Temporão

title: Non-interferometric tests of gravitational decoherence models with mechanical oscillators
abstract: Phenomenological models of quantum-gravity-induced decoherence can leave observable effects even in experiments that do not rely on interferometric measurements. We study three such models, based respectively on deformed relativistic symmetries, stochastic metric fluctuations, and a stochastic generalized uncertainty principle, all of which induce decoherence in the momentum basis. For a free particle, the models preserve momentum distribution and mean energy but produce position diffusion and momentum-space decoherence with model-specific momentum dependences. For a harmonic oscillator, the noncommutativity of the collapse operators with the oscillator Hamiltonian results in anomalous heating, with the three models leading to qualitatively different energy dynamics. The first gives heating at a constant rate, the second at a rate proportional to the kinetic energy, which can lead to exponential growth, and the third at a rate growing cubically with excitation. We further derive the stationary position power spectral density and show that all three models produce the same leading-order excess lineshape in the weak-noise regime, distinct from that of force noise. Comparing with existing mechanical platforms, we find that displacement-noise measurements can already constrain the fluctuation time of the first model below the Planck time, while occupation measurements could improve the bounds on the second model by up to fourteen orders of magnitude over those from ground-state heating of levitated particles. Summing the heating over all phonon modes of a solid, the residual heat release of low-temperature experiments constrains the first model far below the Planck time and the second at the Planck time. Our results establish heating and continuous measurements as complementary non-interferometric probes of gravity-related decoherence.
authors: Sandro Donadi; Iarley P. Lobo; Matteo Fadel

title: Scalable Pauli propagation through $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear partitioning
abstract: Pauli propagation simulates quantum circuits and many-body dynamics by evolving observables in the Heisenberg picture as sparse sums of Pauli strings. As Pauli-string operations reduce to bit manipulations, its performance is limited by memory bandwidth and capacity rather than computational throughput. Pooling the memory of many cores and nodes is hindered by the deduplication step after every gate, which can require global synchronization. We avoid this bottleneck by partitioning the strings with an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear hash function, which guarantees that a $k$-qubit channel couples each partition to at most $4^k$ partitions fixed by the gate, decomposing gate application into independent tasks with bounded communication. Benchmarks of our open-source implementation demonstrate efficient parallel scaling within and across compute nodes, enabling simulations with over $10^{11}$ Pauli strings and extending the accessible timescales of quantum many-body dynamics.
authors: Alev Orfi; Andrew Kille; J. Clayton Peacock; Jack Dunham; Lukas Devos

title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.
authors: Gilberto Borges; Saeid Salari; Ekta Panwar; Samgeeth Puliyil; Kartik Kakade; Peter Rapčan; Mario Ziman; Djeylan Aktas

title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
abstract: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.
authors: Konstantin Beyer; Valentin Link; Surihan Sean Borjigin; Qian Cao; Orion Lee; Kater Murch; Igor Pikovski; Philip Taranto

title: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks
abstract: We investigate boundary-induced stiffness in discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries implemented through coin-flip operations. We define a dimensionless spreading stiffness from the instantaneous variation of the spatial width relative to the asymptotic spreading rate of the corresponding unconfined Hadamard walk and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. The long-time response retains a strong dependence on the initial spatial profile: the localized and truncated-uniform states show an overall increase in stiffness with increasing confinement size, whereas the Gaussian state exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence with a broad maximum at intermediate sizes. The first and second stiffness moments satisfy the expected asymptotic consistency relation in the high-stiffness regime. The normalized Kullback--Leibler divergence reveals a slower spatial reorganization and qualitatively different finite-size trends, showing that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties. These results indicate that unitary confinement produces an intrinsically nonstationary regime whose long-time properties emerge from the interplay between boundary reflections, system size, and the spatial structure of the initial state.
authors: Pablo G. M. Dantas; Rafael Vieira; Edgard P. M. Amorim

title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
abstract: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.
authors: Bowen Xiao; Zhiyao Yang; Huangjun Zhu

title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
abstract: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.
authors: Zhiyao Yang; Bowen Xiao; Huangjun Zhu

title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
abstract: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
authors: Paula I. Villar; Federico Guglielmucci Nazar; Elián Urtubey; Fernando C. Lombardo

title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
abstract: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.
authors: Bibek Saha; David E. Logan; Sthitadhi Roy

title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
authors: Omar Bachain; Mohamed Amazioug; Rachid Ahl Laamara

title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
abstract: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.
authors: Saptarshi Mandal; Sthitadhi Roy

title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
abstract: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.
authors: Anirban Das; Asmi Haldar; Arnab Das

title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
abstract: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.
authors: Xian P. Yang; Christopher T. Parzyck; Martin Cross; Ella Blake; Octave Duros; Yinchuan Lv; Hari Paudyal; Che-Min Lin; Sharon S. title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
abstract: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Here we consider three-level systems, the smallest setting with spacing correlations, and derive exact results for the spread complexity, the Krylov variance, and the Krylov entropy. At infinite temperature, the Krylov basis depends on the spectrum only through the ratio of consecutive level spacings, and the spectral variance enters only as an overall time scale. For Gaussian ensembles, these variables are statistically independent, and the averaged spread complexity and variance reduce to one-dimensional integrals over the spacing-ratio distribution encoding the level statistics. We establish universal late-time values of the complexity and variance, and an algebraic relaxation with exponents set by the Dyson index. We also outline the extension to $d$ levels, with the ensemble-averaged spread complexity expressed as a $(d-2)$-dimensional integral over the joint distribution of consecutive spacing ratios.
authors: Pratik Nandy

title: Quantum violation of Causal Friendliness in the instrumental scenario
abstract: How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal explanations. While generalized notions of causality, capable of incorporating quantum resources, can account for Bell correlations, the Local Friendliness theorem showed that, in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, the conflict between quantum theory and causal explanations persists even after classical causality is abandoned. This revealed a new form of nonclassicality stronger than what was revealed by Bell's theorem. However, Local Friendliness has been confined to Bell causal structures so far, and it remains unknown whether a related form of nonclassicality persists in more general causal networks. Here we answer this question by considering a Wigner's friend version of the instrumental network, a paradigmatic causal structure in which communication between parties is allowed, and, unlike the Bell scenario, relativistic causality does not impose any restriction. We show, both theoretically and in a proof-of-principle photonic experiment, that quantum correlations are incompatible with Causal Friendliness, which is the conjunction of the absoluteness of observed events and the generalized nonclassical causal constraints imposed by the network. Such constraints extend relativistic causality from Bell scenarios to networks of arbitrary structure. These results establish a form of quantum nonclassicality stronger than previously observed in instrumental-network violations of classical causality, generalizing Local Friendliness beyond Bell-Wigner scenarios and uncovering a new class of correlations with potential applications in future quantum technologies.
authors: Emanuele Polino; Giulia Lelli; Aaditya Datar; Marwan Haddara; Davide Poderini; Giorgio Milani; Sergei Slussarenko; Howard M. Wiseman; Nora Tischler; Eric G. Cavalcanti; Fabio Sciarrino

title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

title: Optically-induced electric Aharonov-Bohm effect
abstract: Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, was never experimentally implemented. Here we propose a feasible way to experimentally verify such an important effect, for an electron double-slit interferometer with the slits carved in a nonlinear crystal. The AB phase is generated by a quasi-DC electric field induced in the crystal with the passage of a light pulse (the optical rectification effect) while the electron is superposed in the two slits. We show that this procedure can change the interference pattern of a ensemble of electrons even if they are subjected to negligible electric fields during their propagation, considering feasible parameters.
authors: Gabriel P. Martins; Herman Batelaan; Pablo L. Saldanha

title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.
